name: Massaman Beef curry
assumptions: Yield estimated from typical 600g beef + 450g potatoes + other ingredients for 4 adult main-dish portions, consistent with rice 'to serve' assumption of 75g uncooked per person
Total time is sum of active prep (roasting peanuts 5 min + chopping 5 min + initial frying ~10 min) plus 2-hour oven braise; excludes separate rice cooking
Lime leaves and cinnamon stick treated as non-edible aromatics removed before serving
Massaman curry paste treated as generic commercial Thai paste (may contain shrimp but not confirmed in all brands)
Jasmine rice cooked separately and not included in curry dish itself
No barley/rye/wheat ingredients present; gluten-free status left null due to possible trace gluten in commercial curry paste or fish sauce
No dairy ingredients; dairy-free marked true
No tree nuts, soy, sesame, eggs, milk, or shellfish explicitly listed; soy left null due to possible presence in some curry pastes or sauces
instructions:
Heat oven to 200C/180C fan/gas 6, then roast the peanuts on a baking tray for 5 mins until golden brown. When cool enough to handle, roughly chop. Reduce oven to 180C/160C fan/gas 4.
Heat 2 tbsp coconut cream in a large casserole dish with a lid. Add the curry paste and fry for 1 min, then stir in the beef and fry until well coated and sealed. Stir in the rest of the coconut with half a can of water, the potatoes, onion, lime leaves, cinnamon, tamarind, sugar, fish sauce and most of the peanuts. Bring to a simmer, then cover and cook for 2 hrs in the oven until the beef is tender.
Sprinkle with sliced chilli and the remaining peanuts, then serve straight from the dish with jasmine rice.
